scope: Official Ornith-1.5-9B MLX 4/6/8-bit variants under one representative live Mac workload; one warm-up and one standardized active request per stable model.

ladder.result: stable and fully responsive in this session
stable and fully responsive subjectively, but objectively high pressure
warm-up completed, but server received SIGTERM before stable idle checkpoint; rapid-mlx estimated 13.3 GB working set and warned of 142% utilization

conclusions.comfortable_real_llm_footprint: The largest measured configuration with 0/5 idle and active degradation was official 6-bit: 7.884 GB idle OS footprint, 8.694 GB active OS footprint, and 9.05 GB rapid-mlx Metal peak. This is a session-specific observed maximum, not a universal safe budget.
conclusions.normal_use_maximum: Official 6-bit is the largest tested stable model with 0/5 subjective degradation in this session, but its 11% simulated pressure-free sample and 6.61 GiB post-generation swap make it a high-risk normal configuration rather than a recommended default.
conclusions.heavy_work_budget: No rating-3 boundary was reached. The largest deliberately tolerated configuration was again official 6-bit; 8-bit was not stable enough to classify.
conclusions.practical_ceiling: The practical ceiling was not numerically isolated. It lies below the official 8-bit configuration under this launcher/workload because 8-bit failed stable-server validation. The nearest measured stable point is 9.05 GB Metal peak; the 8-bit warning projected 13.3 GB working set, but those values are not a calibrated threshold pair.
conclusions.base_workload_reserve_required: Not promoted as a single GB number. The live baseline, compression, swap, and process composition varied substantially, and VM categories overlap. A simple 16 GB minus model-file-size calculation is invalid.
conclusions.main_bottleneck: Resident Metal/unified-memory working set and resulting compression/swap pressure, not ordinary RSS. The 4-to-6-bit step added 2,412 MB to active OS footprint and reduced measured decode speed from 7.891 to 4.32 tok/s. The 8-bit configuration crossed rapid-mlx's memory-safety warning regime.
conclusions.confidence: Moderate for relative 4/6/8-bit behavior and the user's ratings in this session; low-to-moderate for generalizing a universal RAM threshold.
remaining_uncertainty: The SIGTERM source during 8-bit warm-up is not proven to be OOM, kernel action, or rapid-mlx self-protection.
Each stable quantization had one warm-up and one active run, not repeated trials.
Swap state was dynamic and not a clean low-load baseline.
The user's live workload may differ across days and application states.
No separate context/KV growth sweep was performed.
No quality or Hermes tool-call evaluation was part of EXP-002.

recommended_next_smallest_experiment: Do not retry 8-bit blindly. First preserve EXP-002 as complete for the primary ladder and, if needed, run a separately approved diagnostic to identify the SIGTERM source with stricter safety limits. For practical Hermes use, treat 4-bit as the robust default and 6-bit as the largest observed high-memory option, pending repeated trials and end-to-end quality/tool-use validation.
